_comment: Research notes for a 'how many packs come in each sealed product' guide, current section plus a historical section. RESEARCH ONLY. Nothing here is wired into a builder yet. Every number carries the source it came from and the date it was read. Anything that could not be sourced is recorded as a gap in `notes` rather than guessed. NO PULL RATES OR ODDS ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE, and none may ever be added: The Pokemon Company does not publish them. Pack counts and card counts are printed on the packaging and are legitimately verifiable, which is why this file is allowed to exist at all.
scope: English / international product unless a row says otherwise. Japanese product is recorded separately and is NOT interchangeable.

confidenceKey.official: Stated on a site run by The Pokemon Company (tcg.pokemon.com, pokemon.com, pokemon-card.com). Safe to publish.
confidenceKey.official+bulbapedia: Same number from an official page AND Bulbapedia. Strongest tier here.
confidenceKey.bulbapedia-2x: Bulbapedia, corroborated on a second independent Bulbapedia page (e.g. the summary article AND the individual set's own page). Still one site, but not one sentence.
confidenceKey.bulbapedia-only: Rests on Bulbapedia alone. Publishable, but the page should say so for these.
confidenceKey.retailer-or-blog-only: Only found on shops, marketplaces or hobby blogs. NOT publishable as stated. Needs a better source or must be left out.
confidenceKey.snippet-only: Seen only in a search-engine summary; the underlying page was never successfully loaded. Treat as a lead, not a fact.

changes.headline: Cards per English booster pack: 11, then 9, then 10. Two clean boundaries, both named.
changes.whyItMatters: This is the fact a buyer of an older sealed pack most needs. An EX-era pack is a smaller pack, not a damaged one.

timeline.gap: Not corroborated on the Base Set or Neo Destiny set pages. The Base Set page was fetched and says nothing about pack contents at all. If this goes on the page, say it rests on Bulbapedia.

timeline.corroborationVerbatim: Each booster pack were reduced from 11 cards to 9 cards; they include 5 Common, 2 Uncommon, 1 Reverse Holofoil, and 1 Rare or Rare Holo card.
timeline.note: The set's own page independently states the 11-to-9 drop, so the boundary is not resting on one sentence. This is also the era that introduced the reverse holo slot.

timeline.verbatim: Since the release of the first Diamond & Pearl expansion, these consistently had 10 cards.
timeline.corroborationVerbatim: Each booster pack were increased from 9 cards to 10 cards; they include 5 Common, 3 Uncommon, 1 Reverse Holofoil, and 1 Rare or Rare Holo card.
timeline.note: Same double-source shape as the Expedition boundary. The 10-card game-card count has not changed since 2007.

timeline.verbatim: Starting in Sun & Moon, internationally released boosters contain one Basic Energy card in addition to the 10 other cards.
timeline.corroborationVerbatim: Each booster pack contained ten cards, plus one Energy card and a code card for the Pokemon Trading Card Game Online.
timeline.corroborationContext: The second quote is the Hidden Fates (2019) set page describing a Sun & Moon-era pack, so it is an independent page confirming the 10 + energy + code shape.

timeline.note: This exact wording appears on the official Journey Together and Destined Rivals expansion pages. It is the safest sentence on the whole page: it is TPCi's own phrasing, and it explains why the physical card count in a modern pack is 11 or 12 while the advertised number is 10.

notes.subject: Sun & Moon pack size
notes.detail: Bulbapedia contradicts itself. The Booster pack (TCG) article says packs held 10 cards from Diamond & Pearl onward and that Sun & Moon added 'one Basic Energy card in addition to the 10 other cards', i.e. 10 game cards, 11 physical. The Sun & Moon (TCG) set page says 'The booster pack size for English expansions were increased from 11 to 12 and included a Basic Energy card in every booster pack', i.e. 11 before and 12 after.
notes.likelyReconciliation: The set page appears to be counting the TCG Online code card as one of the cards: 10 game + 1 code = 11 before, 10 game + 1 energy + 1 code = 12 after. The Hidden Fates page (S5) describes a Sun & Moon-era pack as 'ten cards, plus one Energy card and a code card', which fits that reading exactly.
notes.status: THIS RECONCILIATION IS MY INFERENCE, NOT A SOURCED STATEMENT. No source says the set page is counting the code card. Do not present it as fact.
notes.recommendation: Publish the official wording instead and sidestep the whole thing: TPCi's own current phrasing is '10 cards and 1 Basic Energy' (S9, S11). If the historical row is published, state the 10-game-card count and list the energy and code card as separate extras, and note that some sources count the pack as 11 or 12 depending on whether the extras are included.

notes.subject: Mega Evolution pack contents, July vs August 2025
notes.detail: PokeBeach reported in July 2025 that Mega Evolution packs would contain either an Energy card or a code card but not both, based on the printed booster box fine print. On 2025-08-01 The Pokemon Company clarified that both would continue to be included and that the packaging text was an error.
notes.status: Resolved in favour of the clarification. Recorded because printed boxes carrying the wrong text physically exist, so a buyer can be misled by the product itself.
notes.recommendation: Either omit entirely or state the retraction first. Never state the July version alone.

notes.subject: WotC-era booster box size
notes.detail: No source found for how many packs were in a 1999-2002 booster box. The only booster-box figure found is the general '36' from S1, which is not scoped to a date. Do not write '36 packs since 1999'.

notes.subject: Japanese packs per box
notes.detail: The commonly repeated figure is 30. It was found ONLY on card-shop blogs and marketplace listings, several of which also publish per-box rarity guarantees that this site is forbidden from repeating. The official Japanese page (S18) confirms the 5-card pack size but the box count was not confirmed there. Japanese box sizes also clearly vary by product. Either verify on pokemon-card.com or publish only the pack size.

notes.subject: When the two-pack blister ended
notes.detail: Documented through the Sun & Moon era, absent from Sword & Shield onward. That is an absence of evidence in the merchandise pages, not a sourced discontinuation. Phrase as 'last documented in the Sun & Moon era'.

notes.subject: Theme Deck discontinuation
notes.detail: The Vivid Voltage boundary and the 2021-02-05 first V Battle Deck date come from search summaries only. The fetched Bulbapedia Theme Deck article confirmed neither. Verify on Bulbapedia's 'Theme format (TCG)' page before publishing. What IS solid is the more useful fact: Theme Decks never contained booster packs (S14, S16, two independent pages).

notes.subject: Trainer Kit line
notes.detail: No Bulbapedia article exists at the expected URL. The two data points (DP-era kits included 1 pack, XY-era kits included none) come from era merchandise pages. The last Trainer Kit and the discontinuation date are unsourced.

notes.subject: Base Set 2-Player Starter Set contents
notes.detail: Completely unsourced in this pass. The Base Set page says nothing about it. Do not guess.

notes.subject: 1999-2002 pack count corroboration
notes.detail: The 11-cards-per-pack figure for Base Set through Neo Destiny rests on a single Bulbapedia sentence (S1). Unlike the 9-card and 10-card eras, no individual set page was found repeating it. It is almost certainly right and it is the era buyers of vintage sealed product care about most, so it deserves a second source before publication. Serebii was not successfully consulted in this pass.

notes.subject: Official sources that could not be read
notes.detail: support.pokemon.com returned 403, pokemoncenter.com returned 403 on every product URL, pokebeach.com returned 403. The Pokemon support article 'What can I expect in a Pokemon Trading Card Game booster pack?' is the best single official statement of pack contents and should be opened by hand in a browser before this page ships. Pokemon Center product TITLES were legible in search results and independently support the current figures ('Sleeved Booster Pack (10 Cards)', 'Booster Display Box (36 Packs)', 'Booster Bundle (6 Packs)') but titles are not descriptions.

notes.subject: Where this is strongest and weakest
notes.detail: Strongest: the current-era numbers, which come from three separate official tcg.pokemon.com expansion pages read on 2026-08-15 (Journey Together, Destined Rivals, Mega Evolution) and agree with each other. Also strong: the two cards-per-pack boundaries, each confirmed on both the summary article and the boundary set's own page. Weakest: everything about tins, collection boxes and blisters before 2020, all of which rests on Bulbapedia era merchandise pages alone. That is not a reason to drop them, since Bulbapedia is often the only record, but the page should mark them.

notes.subject: Pull rates
notes.detail: No odds, ratios, per-box guarantees or pull rates are recorded anywhere in this file, and several otherwise usable sources were downgraded specifically because they mix pack counts with rarity guarantees. Rarity-slot breakdowns quoted from Bulbapedia (e.g. '5 Common, 2 Uncommon, 1 Reverse Holofoil, 1 Rare or Rare Holo') describe the PRINTED COMPOSITION of a pack, not the chance of pulling anything. If any of those are published, they must not be framed as odds, and the safer choice is to publish only the totals.
